html:
The Duchy of Schleswig was a duchy in southern Jutland, between the Kingdom of Denmark and Holstein, from the Middle Ages until 1866. It was a Danish fief, ruled in personal union by the Danish king in 1815, while Holstein to its south belonged to the German Confederation.

That mismatch made the Schleswig-Holstein question, one of the knottiest problems of 19th-century Europe. Danish nationalists wanted Schleswig tied to Denmark; German nationalists wanted both duchies together in Germany. The First Schleswig War of 1848 to 1851 left things as they were. In the Second Schleswig War of 1864, Prussia and Austria beat Denmark and took the duchies.

Bismarck then used the quarrel over them to provoke war with Austria in 1866, after which Prussia annexed both. After the First World War, a plebiscite in 1920 returned northern Schleswig to Denmark, and that line is still the border.
